# C29 canonical pin inputs

The C29 integration test compiles the adjacent Lean fixture and rechecks
it through pinned Lean and the fenced ReferenceKernel. The unchanged
pin book `../c29_r4_vi_fenced_pins.json` records SHA-256 digests of the
canonical bincode inputs produced by that run.

This directory holds the actual hashed bytes for every declaration in the
statement, meaning and transitive-closure maps. Each map has its own
directory. The filename is the declaration key in the corresponding map.
The ordinary replay regenerates each byte stream, compares it with the
tracked file, checks the inventory, and compares the independently derived
pin book with the original fixture.

To regenerate the tracked preimages, run the exact C29 test with the
repository-pinned Lean toolchain and
`MINT_X1_R4_VI_FENCED_PREIMAGES=1`. Run the same test without that
environment variable to verify the generated bytes. The preimage
generation mode leaves the pin book intact.
